name: Neural Architecture of Music-Evoked Emotion
short_description: Music-evoked emotions engage distributed network: brainstem (~50ms) → amygdala (~100-200ms) → hippocampus (~500ms-2s) → NAc (~1-5s) → insula → ACC → vmPFC (2-10s); each structure processes different BRECVEMA mechanisms
structural_pattern: Music-evoked emotions engage a distributed network of brain structures, each processing different aspects of the emotional response at different timescales. PROCESSING HIERARCHY: (1) Brainstem nuclei (LC, raphé, reticular formation) — process basic acoustic features, generate arousal responses via noradrenaline/serotonin, ~50ms, implements Juslin's brainstem reflex (B). (2) Amygdala — responds to musical stimuli signaling potential threat (dissonance, unexpected loud sounds), activation modulated by listener familiarity with musical style, ~100-200ms. (3) Hippocampus — dual function: episodic memory retrieval (E-memory mechanism) and novelty/familiarity detection that feeds into prediction error and emotional response, ~500ms-2s. (4) Ventral striatum (NAc) — reward center, produces dopamine during pleasurable moments, receives input from auditory cortex, amygdala, and hippocampus to compute 'reward value', NAc activation proportional to willingness to pay (Salimpoor 2013), ~1-5s. (5) Insula — processes interoceptive signals that constitute 'feeling' of emotion, interface between body's response and subjective experience, connectivity to auditory cortex predicts chill frequency. (6) ACC — monitors conflict between emotional responses. (7) vmPFC/OFC — the familiar subjective value node, integrates prediction outcomes, reward signals, memory associations, and aesthetic evaluations.
higher_order_principle: Music-evoked emotion is not a single neural circuit — it is simultaneous activation of MULTIPLE circuits, each implementing one or more BRECVEMA mechanisms. The temporal unfolding follows the processing hierarchy: fast subcortical mechanisms provide initial affective coloring (~50-100ms), intermediate mechanisms add complexity (~200ms-2s), slow cortical mechanisms produce final evaluative response (~2-10s). vmPFC receives convergent input from all pathways and computes unified subjective value.

brainstem_50ms.structures: Locus coeruleus, raphé nuclei, reticular formation

amygdala_100_200ms.function: Threat/significance detection, aversive response to dissonance

clinical_dissociations.vmpfc_lesion: Intact music perception, impaired music preference (Belfi et al., 2017)
clinical_dissociations.musical_anhedonia: Intact prediction (ERAN normal), absent reward (NAc disconnected)
clinical_dissociations.amygdala_lesion: Impaired recognition of 'scary' music, preserved 'happy' and 'sad' recognition

causal_links.evidence_base: Brainstem responds to sudden loud sounds, rapid onset, extreme frequencies within ~50ms
Salimpoor et al. (2011, 2013) — NAc dopamine release during peak musical pleasure, proportional to willingness to pay
vmPFC appears across all domains as subjective value node (architecture, education, music-pitch, music-rhythm, music-emotion)

scope_conditions: Applies to all music listening with emotional engagement
The full hierarchy engages only for attention-capturing music; background music may engage only lower levels
Individual differences in structural connectivity affect which pathways are most strongly activated
moderators: Musical training enhances auditory cortex and IFG responses
Personal familiarity enhances hippocampal and vmPFC responses
Trait empathy enhances mirror system and insula responses

interactions.nature: M12 provides the psychological mechanism taxonomy; M13 provides the neural implementation
